unchanged_count.reason: The remaining obligation changed materially: breadth beyond Chen-Li/easy matching is now discharged by a dense vertex-relabeling graph mixture with an exact primitive-pressure proof, and prior-art checking identifies that instantiation as classical. The remaining work is audit completion plus folklore/cluster-expansion collision testing and, if novelty survives, a genuinely new instantiation.

methods.B7: Derived the exact Eulerian-subgraph partition function for a dense Rademacher two-community graph mixture, reduced it to one-dimensional magnetization pressure, proved a uniform second-moment bound below q=1, and obtained the sharp finite-pressure limit.
methods.B19: Turned the proof into an explicit parameter-level certification procedure using c=n*arctanh(rho^2 lambda^2/n), avoiding enumeration of high-degree Eulerian supports.
methods.B23: Showed complete low-interface factorization is not necessary: long simple cycles are indecomposable positive atoms but bounded low-degree advantage still implies full statistical hardness; introduced the primitive-pressure plus composite-interface hybrid viewpoint.

new_mathematical_results: Exact Fourier rule for the dense Rademacher two-community graph mixture: coefficients are (lambda/sqrt(n))^|S| exactly on Eulerian edge sets and zero otherwise.
Exact finite-n pressure identity Z_n(t)=(1-t^2)^{N/2} exp(-n arctanh(t)/2) E exp(arctanh(t) M_n^2/2), with Z_n(q/n) <= (1-n arctanh(q/n))^{-1/2} when the denominator is positive.

Source-style proposition: if D_n->infinity, D_n=o(sqrt(n)), and low-degree advantage is uniformly bounded through D_n, then limsup lambda_n^2<1; consequently full pre-noise chi-square is uniformly bounded and no measurable strong distinguisher exists.
Primitive-cycle tail bound R_D <= q^{D+1}/(2(D+1)(1-q)) for q<1.
Hybrid primitive/composite reassembly lemma recorded as equation (7.2) in the report.
failed_routes: Complete low-interface factorization is not necessary because a simple cycle has no proper nonempty Eulerian positive sub-atom.
Naive geometric summation over cycle decompositions loses enough structure that it is non-sharp before the true q=1 dense-SBM threshold.
The dense-SBM hardness conclusion is not novel; Banerjee and Banerjee-Ma already establish the underlying contiguity/signed-cycle phenomenon.
